GUIDE FOR SELECTION OF ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT FOR COAL MINES

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 July 1980, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Apparatus for Explosive Atmospheres Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 Though a number of standards have been published for the techniques of protection of electrical equipment in hazardous areas, yet the only protection that is still acceptable for the use of electrical and electronic equipment in hazardous locations of coal mines is the technique of flameproof enclosures and intrinsically safe circuits and equipment. It has is not fully applicable for selection of been felt that IS : 5571-1979* equipment in coal mines. As such, a separate standard in this respect may be useful for selection of proper equipment for use in coal mines. 0.3 While preparing this guide it has been borne in mind that all coal mines in India have been classified as gassy mines. Depending on the rate of emission of the flammable gas ( methane ) the coal seams have been classified in three degrees ( see 2 ). 0.4 In selecting electrical equipments other than the flameproof, a number of considerations have to be taken into account keeping in view the common hazards like risks of roof fall or fall of other materials, coal dust, moisture, water, vermin, etc, encountered in the underground situations In such cases where use of flameproof equipments is not of a coal mine. statutorily or otherwise required, other techniques of protection such aa type of protection ` e' may be selected subject to the approval of approving authority. The equipment prescribed above shall offer reasonable degree of protection against the common hazards in underground situations of a coal mine. Equipment with type of protection ` e ' shall not be considered case as an alternative to flameproof equipment. in any

*Guide for selection of electrical equipment for hazardous areas (PM revision ). 3

KS$9559 - 1980 0.5 While preparing this standard, the statutory regulations in this country have been kept in mind. However, if there is a conflict between statutory regulations in force in any area and this standard, the provisions of the former will prevail. 0.6 The statutory authority in India, for approval of equipment in coal mines is the Director General Mines Safety, Dhanbad. ior use

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard gives guidance for selection of electrical and electronic equipment for use in the underground situations of coal mines in general and the permissibility of the ordinary equipment, flameproof equipment and the intrinsically safe equipment in particular. 2. CLASSIFICATION 2.0 For the purpose mines shall apply. OF COAL MINES of this guide, the following classification of coal

2.1 Gassy Seam of Degree I - A coal seam or part thereof lying within the precincts of a mine not being an open cast working whether or not flammable gas is actually detected in the general body of the air at any place in its workings below ground or when the percentage of the inflammable gas, if and when detected, in such general body of air does not exceed 0.1 and the rate of emission of such gas does not exceed 1 ma per tonne of coal produced. 2.2 Gassy Seam of Degree II - A coal seam or part thereof lying within the precincts of a mine not being an open cast working in which the percentage of flammable gas in the general body of air at any place in the workings of the seam is more than O,l or the rate of emission of flammable gas per tonne of coal produced exceeds 1 m* but does not exceed 10 ma. 2.3 Gassy Seam of Degree III - A coal seam or part thereof lying within the precincts of a mine not .being an open cast working in which the rate of emission of flammable gas tonne of coal produced exceeds 10 ms. 3. GENERAL 3.0 The equipments generally used below ground in coal mines are for the following purposes: a) Electric power supply, transmission, 4 distribution and use; b) Transportation of men, mineral and material;

5. CONTROLGEAR 5.1 Enclosure - Ail underground controlgears shall be robust in construction and suitable for rough usage except in cases where such control gears are required to be flameproof which shall be of a type approved by the Director General of Mines Safety. - The control gears shall have the following 5.2 Protection features and shall be of appropriate rupturing capacity: protective

a) Overload protection, b) Short-circuit protection, c) Earth leakage protection with built-in testing device and re-setting device which may be operated externally, tl) Interlocked earthing of the outgoing circuit at 3*3 kV and above, e) Suitable interlocks for opening the main cover, f) No voltage protection for starters, and g) Zener barrier protection for intrinsically safe circuits. 6. TRANSFORMERS 6.1 The transformers shall be in flameproof construction where statutorily required and shall be of a approved type. For protection of the transformers, suitable circuit-breakers shall be installed both on primary and secondary sides. All transformers shall have their secondary windings star connected to facilitate earthing of the neutral point. In case undergrounded neutral system is used, arrangement of insulation monitoring along with suitable visual and audible signal shall be provided so as to mdicatc th: fLril of insulation below a predetermined level. 6.2 Transformers which are provided with isolation plates to prevent connections between the intrinsically safe and non-intrinsically safe circuits shall have the following features: a) In case the terminals of the transformers are exposed, the distance between the other winding terminals shall be more than 50 mm so as to prcvcnt any contact between them. Alternatively, the exposed terminals shall be covered by insulation. b) The copper plate used as isolation plate shall have a thickness not less than 0.1 mm. The contact plate shall be located in such a way that there is no possibility of any contact with the windings. c) The insulation of the primary winding shail be capable of withstanding a test voltage of 2500 V ( rms ) for 1 minute when applied between winding and the isolation plate. Similarly, the insulation of the secondary winding shall withstand a test voltage of 1 500 V rms for 1 minute between the winding and isolation plate. 6

IS : 9559 d) It shall be ensurctl, in case the winding no unwinding of the coil. 7. INSULATED 7.1 The cables CABLES for various application in coal mints should wire breaks,

9. POWER

DISTRIBUTION
special features in the underground power distribution

9.1 The following
should be achieved:

a) All sub-circuits are controlled individually by a circuit-breaker so as to protect the circuit from heating under overload conditions which may occur by the various working conditions or the fault conditions. b) The arrangement of sub-circuits should be such that isolating the branch is readily possible without affecting the healthy branches and easily carry out the repairs to the faulty branch without causing any undesirable consequences such as electric shock, spark or explosion, etc.
C)

Protective devices are so asranged and graded that the faulty circuit is automatically isolated and prevented from being energized by an unauthorised person.

10. MOTORS

AND

MOTOR

STARTERS

be used subject to the approval of the approving authority.

10.1 Motors -AC squirrel cage or slip ring motors are usually employed for system voltages of 415, 550 and 330 V. Selection of the motor is decided by the job requirement. The requirement of flameproof construction or otherwise is to be determined by the safety regulations. In situations where the use of flameproof equipment is not statutorily required, other types of protection, such as type of protection ` e ' may

10.2 Gate End Circuit-Breakers - Motor starters are sometimes required to be installed at the gate end of a working face and have been designated as Gate End boxes. The requirement of flameproofness is guided by safety regulations. Speciality of construction is dependent upon job requirement. But the following protective features should generally be adopted: a) A separate flameproof isolating chamber with an off-load isolator, b) Conductors of suitable mechanical and electrical duty class, 8 duty class utilization category

12.1.2 Coal Cutting kfachines - The machines consist of a flameproof motor and controller and is connected to its controlgear by a screened flexible cable with plug and socket assembly. The controlgear and flexible cable used shall be of approved type and complying with IS : 6911966*. The controlgear is intended to be operated on remote control so that pilot core protection could be provided. 12.1.3 Continuous Miner, Shearer and Plough - These machines are used for complete coal mining without any need of blasting. Continuous miner is used for board and piller and room and piller system. Shearers and ploughs are used in long wall system. The electrical system and arrangement should be similar to loader/shuttle, car. The hydraulic oil, lubricant, etc, should be fire resistant type. Safety chain/rope should be provided to prevent the machine slide away in case of failure of the propelling arrangement.

SIGNALLING

AND

TELECOMMUNICATION
shall be carried out by intrinsically

13.1 Signalling safe equipment

and telecommunication and circuits.

13.2 Signalling is normally done for the operation of haulage units through two bare wires supported on insulators andrunning on the haulage plane. Anywhere from the haulage plane, the signalling should be effected by the operator by short-circuiting the two bare wires. This signalling may be of ringing type or hooter type and usually employs a signalling bell transformer of primary 120 V and secondary15 V. Only the secondary side of transformer need be intrinsically safe and primary side may, therefore, be made only flameproof.
X3.3 Telecommunication is usually provided between the shaft top and shaft bottom and is also essential for the purpose of stowing operation. The telephones ( see IS : 6539-1972t ) may be of dynamo operated ringing circuit and battery operated hearing circuit. The other form may be This system is using battery circuit only with the help of electronics. preferred. The battery voltage usually is between 6.and 9 V providing a dependable intrinsically safe system when designed carefu!ly. 13.4 Intrinsically safe loud hailers and electronic communication circuits may be used, working both on 110 V ac supply and with re-chargeable Battery life should be sufficient to cater battery in case of power failure. power requirements for a week.

ILLUMINATION in the underground situation of a mine is also very important particularly at the working faces and at important traffic junctions where tubes are attached or detached. This is a statutory requirement that all lighting fittings shall be of flameprcof construction only. 14.2 The voltage of the lights should be limited to 110 V with a special system construction so that if the electric supply be single-phase the mid point of the system shall be connected to earth or if the supply be threephase the voltage between the phases shall not exceed 110 V and the neutral point of the system shall be earthed. 14.3 Ordinary junction boxes or connectors are not required in the lighting installations as the flameproof lighting fitting is so constructed that it may be operated as a single-way, two-way, three-way or four-way connector. 14.4 Two core having metallic 15. copper cable with PVC ineulaticn or paper insulaticn armculing earthed shculd be used for lighting fittings. DE-WATERING

15.1 This problem has peculiar features deper.ding on the type of the mine. In case of a quarry, the free run of water from the surface of the mine may be huge. If it is an incline all round percolation frcm the surface may attain a large value alcng with the possibilities of water running into the mine through the incline mouths. In shaft mining there is possibility of huge percolation within the shaft itself alcng with the percolation from the roofs and walls of the mines. For complete dewatering of the mine the pumping system may be divided into the following groups: a) Main pumps at the pit bottom for pumping main sump to the surface of the mine. b) water from a large

Stage pum,ps installed at different stages of the mine with comparatively limited sump capacity. The stage pumps discharge water to the main sump. water main from sump

c) Comparatively smaller pumps may be used to pump the working faces to the stage pumps or even to the depending on the development of the mine. 15.2 The rate of accumulation of water in seasonal variation and, therefore, a number desirable. One or more main pumps may requirement. 12

15.3 The output of the motors for main pumps may be between 55 and 445 kW depending on the depth of the shaft. Properly designed squirrel cage motors with direct-on-line starters both of flameproof construction may be employed. Depending on the ventilation and proximity of working faces or goaf, totally enclosed fan-cooled motors may also be permitted. There is, however, no objection to the use of properly constructed slip-ring induction motors with suitable controlgears. Slip-ring induction motors may be more suitable with higher output and high head
pump. 15.4 Output of the stage pumps may be between and a squirrel cage induction motor with proper the purpose. 15 and 75 kW normally enclosure usually serves

15.5 Selection of face pumps should be done very judiciously keeping in view the different problems encountered at the coal face. Generally squirrel cage motors of output 3.7 to 11 kW are used to run centrifugal pump at the face. These are generally low-read pumps pumping water from face to the nearest sump. 15.6 Submersible pumps water from coal faces. 16. are considered extremely suitable for pumping
